correctness.rationale: The Fourier basis and moment ratios give a bilateral invertible weighted shift converging compactly to the bilateral unitary. Its lack of off-circle eigenvectors and index zero identify its spectrum. Direct projection gives the sole defect delta=m1(rho−1) at e_-1 to e_1. Exact resolvent matrix entries by root location yield an exhaustive rank-one determinant; the mixed-root condition v=rho*u supplies the unique outlier, with nonzero derivative giving algebraic simplicity. Every beta and singular example is computed from exact moments. 2,182 additional rational finite checks were replayed but not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: A complete natural all-radial-measures spectral classification depends on only one ratio of two moments, not the infinitely many higher moments. It produces exact isospectrality between a singular boundary/atom law and continuous area law and an explicitly weight-controlled creation of an isolated eigenvalue for a fixed polynomial. These are meaningful model-comparison and spectral-topology phenomena beyond the known fixed-unweighted quadratic result.
